# Expression functions

<!-- GENERATED by `zig build docs-md` from the FnDoc catalog in expr.zig. Do not edit. -->

All function names are case-insensitive. Functions are grouped by purpose
below; each table sorts on a header click and filters as you type.

## Logic & conditionals

Branch, fall back to the first non-empty value, and test membership.

| Function                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">IF</span>(cond, yes, no)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">IF</span>(<span class="hl-num">1</span> &lt; <span class="hl-num">0</span>, <span class="hl-str">'yes'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'no'</span>)</code>                                                                                                                                            | Short-circuit conditional. Returns `yes` if `cond` is truthy, else `no`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">CASE</span>(expr, m<span class="hl-num">1</span>, r<span class="hl-num">1</span>, …, default)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">CASE</span>(<span class="hl-str">'B'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'B'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'BUY'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'S'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'SELL'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'?'</span>)</code> | Multi-branch mapping. Compares `expr` against each `m`/`r` pair in order and returns the first matching `r`; returns the trailing `default` when nothing matches (or "" if no default is given). Equality matches the `=` operator (numeric when both sides parse as numbers, else byte-exact string). Only the selected result is evaluated. Collapses nested `IF(IF(IF(…)))` chains. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">IFERROR</span>(expr, fallback)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">IFERROR</span>(YEAR(<span class="hl-str">'not-a-date'</span>), <span class="hl-str">''</span>)</code>                                                                                                                                                                                        | Return `expr`'s value, or `fallback` if evaluating `expr` raises a data error (not-a-number, bad date, numeric overflow). `fallback` is evaluated only on error. Template errors — unknown function, wrong argument count, syntax — are NOT caught: IFERROR guards against messy data, not template mistakes.                                                                          |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">COALESCE</span>(a, b, ...)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">COALESCE</span>(<span class="hl-str">''</span>, <span class="hl-str">'fallback'</span>)</code>                                                                                                                                                                                                   | First non-empty argument (empty = whitespace-only string). Returns last argument verbatim as fallback.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">NULLIF</span>(value, sentinel)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">NULLIF</span>(<span class="hl-str">'N/A'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'N/A'</span>)</code>                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Return `""` when `value` equals `sentinel`, otherwise return `value`. Equality is numeric when both sides parse as numbers, otherwise byte-exact string compare — mirrors the `=` operator. Typical use: collapse sentinel values such as `"-9999"`, `"\N"`, `"N/A"` to empty.                                                                                                         |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">IN</span>(value, v<span class="hl-num">1</span>, v<span class="hl-num">2</span>, ...)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">IN</span>(<span class="hl-str">'BUY'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'BUY'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'SELL'</span>)</code>                                                                                                            | Return "true" when `value` equals any of `v1, v2, …`. Equality is numeric when both sides parse as numbers, otherwise byte-exact string compare — mirrors the `=` operator. Variadic 2+ args.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">ISEMPTY</span>(x)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">ISEMPTY</span>(<span class="hl-str">' '</span>)</code>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Return "true" when `x` is empty or whitespace-only, else "false". The safe emptiness test: a bare `x = ''` wrongly matches `'0'` (which coerces to empty in numeric context), whereas ISEMPTY checks the trimmed string length.                                                                                                                                                        |

## Text

Trim, case-fold, slice, pad, search, and measure strings.

| Function                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">TRIM</span>(f)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">TRIM</span>(<span class="hl-str">' hello '</span>)</code>                                                                                       | Strip leading and trailing whitespace from a string.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">SPLIT_PART</span>(s, delim, n)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">SPLIT_PART</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL.US'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'.'</span>, <span class="hl-num">1</span>)</code> | Return the n-th part of `s` split by `delim` (1-based index). Returns "" when n exceeds the part count, when `delim` is empty, or when `n` ≤ 0. When `delim` is not found, n=1 returns the whole string and n>1 returns "".                                                                               |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">CONTAINS</span>(haystack, needle)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">CONTAINS</span>(<span class="hl-str">'Apple Inc'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'Inc'</span>)</code>                           | Returns "true" if `haystack` contains `needle`, else "false".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">LEFT</span>(s, n)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">LEFT</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL.US'</span>, <span class="hl-num">4</span>)</code>                                                     | Return the first `n` bytes of `s`. `n` is clamped to `[0, len(s)]`; negative `n` returns "".                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">RIGHT</span>(s, n)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">RIGHT</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL.US'</span>, <span class="hl-num">2</span>)</code>                                                   | Return the last `n` bytes of `s`. `n` is clamped to `[0, len(s)]`; negative `n` returns "".                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">SUBSTR</span>(s, start, length)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">SUBSTR</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL.US'</span>, <span class="hl-num">1</span>, <span class="hl-num">4</span>)</code>      | Return `length` bytes from `s` starting at 1-based position `start`. Returns "" when `start` is non-positive / past end of `s`, or when `length` is negative. `length` is clamped to the bytes remaining from `start`.                                                                                    |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">UPPER</span>(s)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">UPPER</span>(<span class="hl-str">'aapl'</span>)</code>                                                                                        | Full-Unicode upper-case conversion: works across Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, etc. (café → CAFÉ, ß → SS); unicameral scripts (CJK, Arabic, Hebrew) pass through unchanged. Invalid UTF-8 bytes pass through verbatim.                                                                                          |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">LOWER</span>(s)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">LOWER</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL'</span>)</code>                                                                                        | Full-Unicode lower-case conversion: works across Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, etc. (CAFÉ → café, Я → я); unicameral scripts (CJK, Arabic, Hebrew) pass through unchanged. Invalid UTF-8 bytes pass through verbatim.                                                                                           |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">UNACCENT</span>(s)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">UNACCENT</span>(<span class="hl-str">'Café Crème'</span>)</code>                                                                            | Strip diacritics from Latin text (café → cafe, ÀÉÎ → AEI, ß → ss, ø → o). Latin-scope like Postgres unaccent: non-Latin letters keep their base script (Greek Ά → Α, not A) and CJK/Arabic pass through unchanged; ligatures are NOT folded. Invalid UTF-8 bytes pass through verbatim.                   |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">STARTS_WITH</span>(s, prefix)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">STARTS_WITH</span>(<span class="hl-str">'US123'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'US'</span>)</code>                                 | Return "true" when `s` begins with `prefix` (case-sensitive byte match), else "false". An empty `prefix` always matches.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">ENDS_WITH</span>(s, suffix)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">ENDS_WITH</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL.PR'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'.PR'</span>)</code>                                  | Return "true" when `s` ends with `suffix` (case-sensitive byte match), else "false". An empty `suffix` always matches.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">LEN</span>(s)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">LEN</span>(<span class="hl-str">'hello'</span>)</code>                                                                                           | Byte length of `s` (UTF-8 byte count, not codepoint or grapheme count). Empty string → 0.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">LPAD</span>(s, len, pad)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">LPAD</span>(<span class="hl-str">'42'</span>, <span class="hl-num">5</span>, <span class="hl-str">'0'</span>)</code>                  | Left-pad `s` with the `pad` string (repeated, then clipped) until it is `len` bytes long. If `s` is already `len` or longer it is truncated to the first `len` bytes; an empty `pad` returns `s` unchanged. `len` is clamped to [0, 65535]. Byte-based (UTF-8 byte count).                                |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">RPAD</span>(s, len, pad)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">RPAD</span>(<span class="hl-str">'42'</span>, <span class="hl-num">5</span>, <span class="hl-str">' '</span>)</code>                  | Right-pad `s` with the `pad` string (repeated, then clipped) until it is `len` bytes long. If `s` is already `len` or longer it is truncated to the first `len` bytes; an empty `pad` returns `s` unchanged. `len` is clamped to [0, 65535]. Byte-based (UTF-8 byte count).                               |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">POSITION</span>(needle, haystack)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">POSITION</span>(<span class="hl-str">'Inc'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'Apple Inc'</span>)</code>                           | 1-based byte position of the first occurrence of `needle` inside `haystack`, or 0 when not found. An empty `needle` returns 1. Byte-based (UTF-8 byte offset), case-sensitive.                                                                                                                            |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">PROPER</span>(s)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">PROPER</span>(<span class="hl-str">'apple inc'</span>)</code>                                                                                 | Title-case `s`: upper-case the first letter of every word and lower-case the rest (`apple inc` → `Apple Inc`, `o'brien` → `O'Brien`). Words break on any non-letter (spaces, digits, punctuation), like Excel PROPER. Full-Unicode via the same case tables as UPPER/LOWER; invalid UTF-8 passes through. |

## Pattern matching

Linear-time (ReDoS-safe) regular-expression match and extract.

| Function                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">REGEX_MATCH</span>(s, pattern)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">REGEX_MATCH</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL US Equity'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'[A-Z]+'</span>)</code>                     | Returns "true" if regular-expression `pattern` matches anywhere in `s`, else "false". `pattern` is a regex literal: anchors `^ $`, classes `[...]`, quantifiers `* + ? {m,n}`, groups, and alternation `\|` — linear-time (no backreferences or lookaround). Unicode-scalar mode is on, so `.` and class ranges span whole code points, but `\d`/`\w`/`\s` stay ASCII — match accented letters with an explicit class like `[A-ZÁ-Ž]`. Pay for the cheapest tool that does the job: CONTAINS for a literal substring, IN/REMAP for whole-value sets, regex only for a real pattern. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">REGEX_EXTRACT</span>(s, pattern)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">REGEX_EXTRACT</span>(<span class="hl-str">'Qualified Dividend AAPL 100'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'[A-Z]{2,}'</span>)</code> | Returns the first part of `s` that regular-expression `pattern` matches, or "" if there is no match. When `pattern` has a capture group `(...)`, the first group's text is returned; otherwise the whole match is returned. `pattern` is a regex literal (same syntax + Unicode notes as REGEX_MATCH): linear-time, no backreferences or lookaround, and accented letters need an explicit class like `[A-ZÁ-Ž]` (not `\w`). Use it to pull a ticker, code, or token a literal REPLACE/SPLIT_PART cannot isolate.                                                                   |

## Lookup & mapping

Whole-value remap, substring replace, and `pre_pass` table lookups.

| Function                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">REMAP</span>(s, <span class="hl-str">'name'</span> &#124; k, v, ...)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">REMAP</span>(<span class="hl-str">'VOW.DE'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'VOW.DE'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'VOW.DE.XETRA'</span>)</code>                                                            | Whole-value lookup: if `s` exactly equals a map key, return that key's value, else return `s` unchanged. Named form REMAP(s, 'mapname') resolves a `maps` registry entry; inline form REMAP(s, k1,v1, k2,v2, ...) gives the pairs directly. The whole-value sibling of REPLACE (which matches substrings) — use it to remap broker symbols, codes or enum values.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">LOOKUP</span>([name,] key, field)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">LOOKUP</span>(<span class="hl-str">'AAPL'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'name'</span>)</code>                                                                                                                                              | Retrieve a value stored by a pre_pass table. 3-arg form `LOOKUP(name, key, field)` selects the named pre_pass block. 2-arg form `LOOKUP(key, field)` works only when exactly one pre_pass block is defined.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">REPLACE</span>(s, <span class="hl-str">'name'</span> &#124; from, to, ...)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">REPLACE</span>(<span class="hl-str">'1 234,56'</span>, <span class="hl-str">' '</span>, <span class="hl-str">''</span>, <span class="hl-str">','</span>, <span class="hl-str">'.'</span>)</code> | Replace substrings in `s`. Named form REPLACE(s, 'mapname') applies a `maps` registry entry's pairs. Inline single-pair REPLACE(s, from, to) replaces every occurrence of `from` with `to` (case-sensitive byte match, so multi-byte UTF-8 needles work — this is substring replace, not char-by-char). Inline variadic REPLACE(s, from1, to1, from2, to2, ...) applies the pairs in one left-to-right pass: at each position the first pair (in declared order) whose `from` matches wins and the emitted `to` is not re-scanned, so one pass replaces several tokens at once without nesting. An empty `from` matches nothing. Whole-value sibling: REMAP. |

## Numbers & money

Exact fixed-point arithmetic, rounding, min/max, and price parsing.

| Function                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">ABS</span>(f)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">ABS</span>(-<span class="hl-num">12.5</span>)</code>                                                                             | Absolute numeric value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">ROUND</span>(f, n)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">ROUND</span>(<span class="hl-num">3.14159</span>, <span class="hl-num">2</span>)</code>                                     | Round `f` to `n` decimal places (half away from zero, like Excel: `ROUND(2.5,0)=3`). `n=0` rounds to the nearest integer; `n<0` rounds to tens/hundreds/etc. (`n=-2` → nearest 100); `n>=12` is a no-op (12 is the fixed-point scale). `n` is clamped to ±30.        |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">FLOOR</span>(f)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">FLOOR</span>(<span class="hl-num">3.7</span>)</code>                                                                           | Round `f` down to nearest integer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">CEILING</span>(f)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">CEILING</span>(<span class="hl-num">3.2</span>)</code>                                                                       | Round `f` up to nearest integer.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">RAND</span>(n)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">RAND</span>(<span class="hl-num">8</span>)</code>                                                                               | A string of exactly `n` random digits (each position 0–9, except the first which is 1–9 so a leading zero can't be dropped by a downstream numeric import). Use it for synthetic IDs; `n` is clamped to [1, 65]. Cryptographically seeded — not for security tokens. |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">PRICE_VALUE</span>(f)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">PRICE_VALUE</span>(<span class="hl-str">'$1,234.56'</span>)</code>                                                       | Strip currency symbol or code from a price string, return the numeric part (e.g. "$88744.27" → "88744.27", "€24.00" → "24.00", "24.00 CZK" → "24.00").                                                                                                               |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">PRICE_CURRENCY</span>(f)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">PRICE_CURRENCY</span>(<span class="hl-str">'$1,234.56'</span>)</code>                                                 | Extract currency code from a price string (e.g. "EUR", "USD").                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">GREATEST</span>(a, b, ...)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">GREATEST</span>(<span class="hl-num">3</span>, <span class="hl-num">7</span>, <span class="hl-num">5</span>)</code> | Largest numeric value among arguments. Per-row maximum (not aggregation across rows). Arguments are coerced to numbers; empty string coerces to 0, non-numeric strings raise an error.                                                                               |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">LEAST</span>(a, b, ...)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">LEAST</span>(<span class="hl-num">3</span>, <span class="hl-num">7</span>, <span class="hl-num">5</span>)</code>       | Smallest numeric value among arguments. Per-row minimum (not aggregation across rows). Arguments are coerced to numbers; empty string coerces to 0, non-numeric strings raise an error.                                                                              |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">MOD</span>(a, b)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">MOD</span>(<span class="hl-num">7</span>, <span class="hl-num">3</span>)</code>                                               | Remainder of `a` divided by `b`, with the sign of the dividend `a` (truncated division, like SQL/C `%`: `MOD(-7, 3) = -1`). `MOD(a, 0)` returns "" (mirrors the `/` operator's silent divide-by-zero). Exact over the fixed-point decimal core.                      |

## Dates & time

Reformat, shift, diff, and decompose dates — business-day aware.

| Function                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">NOW</span>()</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">NOW</span>()</code>                                                                                                                                                              | Current UTC datetime as ISO 8601 string (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">DATE_CONVERT</span>(f, from, to)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">DATE_CONVERT</span>(<span class="hl-str">'31.12.2024'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'DD.MM.YYYY'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'YYYY-MM-DD'</span>)</code>     | Reformat a date/time string. Format tokens: YYYY (year), MM/M (month), MMM/MMMM (month name), DD/D (day), hh/h (hour), mm/m (minute), ss/s (second), [literal] (literal characters), [*] (wildcard).                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">DATEADD</span>(d, n)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">DATEADD</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-01-31'</span>, <span class="hl-num">7</span>)</code>                                                                           | Add `n` calendar days to date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD). Negative `n` subtracts. Returns YYYY-MM-DD. For business-day arithmetic (skipping weekends) use WORKDAY().                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">DATEDIFF</span>(d<span class="hl-num">1</span>, d<span class="hl-num">2</span>)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">DATEDIFF</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-01-01'</span>, <span class="hl-str">'2024-12-31'</span>)</code>    | Calendar days from `d2` to `d1`: positive when `d1` is later. Both arguments are YYYY-MM-DD strings.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">WORKDAY</span>(d, n)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">WORKDAY</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-01-01'</span>, <span class="hl-num">10</span>)</code>                                                                          | Add `n` business days to date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD), skipping Saturdays and Sundays. Negative `n` subtracts. Correct for T+2 settlement math; does NOT account for exchange holidays.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">YEAR</span>(d)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">YEAR</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-03-15'</span>)</code>                                                                                                                   | Year component of date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD) as a number.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">MONTH</span>(d)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">MONTH</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-03-15'</span>)</code>                                                                                                                 | Month component of date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD) as a number, 1-12.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">DAY</span>(d)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">DAY</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-03-15'</span>)</code>                                                                                                                     | Day-of-month component of date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD) as a number, 1-31.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">WEEKDAY</span>(d)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">WEEKDAY</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-03-15'</span>)</code>                                                                                                             | ISO day-of-week for date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD): Monday=1 … Sunday=7. Useful for weekend-trade detection: `WEEKDAY([Date]) > 5`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">EOMONTH</span>(d)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">EOMONTH</span>(<span class="hl-str">'2024-02-10'</span>)</code>                                                                                                             | Last calendar day of the month containing date `d` (YYYY-MM-DD), as YYYY-MM-DD. Useful for snapping coupon/dividend dates and month-end reporting.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">NTH_DOW</span>(year, month, weekday, n)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">NTH_DOW</span>(<span class="hl-num">2024</span>, <span class="hl-num">3</span>, <span class="hl-num">7</span>, -<span class="hl-num">1</span>)</code> | Date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the `n`-th `weekday` (ISO Mon=1 … Sun=7) in `year`/`month`. Positive `n` counts from the start (1 = first); negative counts from the end (-1 = last). Returns "" when the occurrence doesn't exist or an argument is out of range. Handy for DST boundaries — EU summer time is `NTH_DOW(YEAR(d), 3, 7, -1)` (last Sunday of March) to `NTH_DOW(YEAR(d), 10, 7, -1)` (last Sunday of October). |

## Row & source context

Values drawn from the current row's position and its source file.

| Function                                                                                                                                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">FIELDS</span>(n)</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">FIELDS</span>(<span class="hl-num">2</span>)</code> | Field value by 1-based column index. n must be a positive integer — use this when the column header is unknown or unstable; use the [ColumnName] syntax to look up by header name.                                                                                                                                                |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">FILENAME</span>()</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">FILENAME</span>()</code>                           | Input file stem — the file name with its directory and the matched `file_pattern_in` suffix removed (the same stem used for output naming). Broker exports often encode account/broker/period in the name, so e.g. `SPLIT_PART(FILENAME(), '_', 3)` extracts a field from it. Empty during stateless evaluation (no source file). |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">RECORD_NUM</span>()</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">RECORD_NUM</span>()</code>                       | 1-based input record number of the current row within the file (the first data row is 1). Use it for synthetic IDs, dedup keys, or skip-first-N logic. 0 during stateless evaluation and inside the pre_pass scan.                                                                                                                |
| <code><span class="hl-fn">SHEET_NAME</span>()</code><br><code class="fn-eg"><span class="hl-fn">SHEET_NAME</span>()</code>                       | For xlsx-derived input, the configured `xlsx_sheet.name` the row came from; "" for native CSV/JSON input and during stateless evaluation.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
